How it works

  • Every day there's one battle: your team (given, not built) against a gym leader, played by FireRed's own battle code.
  • Goal: win without losing a Pokémon. You pick every move and switch; the leader plays with the game's own trainer AI.
  • Every attempt rolls fresh dice. Attempt 2 has the same dice for everyone, and so on, so you can compare with friends.
  • Your score is about your choices, not the dice. At each turn the engine plays out every option many times and measures how much of your chance of a clean win each one gives up. Most turns have several good options; a choice is only marked when it clearly gives up a chunk: Mistake 10–25 points, Blunder over 25.
  • You kept X of Y%: Y is the chance of a clean win from the start with strong play. Each marked choice scales it by how much of the best option's chance it kept (a choice that leaves half the chance halves it); unmarked choices keep it all. Whether the dice then went your way is shown separately, as luck.
  • After a battle, Strong play shows the engine's strongest search playing the whole fight on your dice, with its plan and your choices side by side. Attempts after watching it are marked 👀.
  • Once one of your Pokémon faints the goal is gone, so the rest of that battle isn't graded.
  • The grades are estimates from simulated battles: good at spotting big mistakes, not exact to the point.
  • The Damage calculator under your moves shows what each of their Pokémon (including ones not out yet) does to any of yours and back, with the game's own damage code. The + / − buttons try stat changes, like "what if I use Harden four times first". It also lists who moves first: every Pokémon's speed as the game's turn order uses it, with speed changes and paralysis you can try.
  • After a battle, Why? next to a marked choice shows how the choices compared on the same dice, what usually went wrong, and lets you watch the better option played out: with your dice, or on a battle where it made the difference. The lucky breaks each side got are counted, so a line that only won on a crit says so.
